translation: (Zhuye Tang.) When the moving qi is on the left, one must not cause sweating; if one sweats it, there will be dizziness, sweating that does not stop, and twitching of the sinews and quivering of the flesh; this is difficult to treat; (or first use Fangfeng Baizhu Muli Tang, then Xiao Jianzhong Tang) one must not purge; if one purges it, the abdomen will be cramped and not stop, the moving qi will instead become severe, and although the body has heat, one instead wants to curl up. (First take Gancao Ganjiang Tang, then take Xiao Jianzhong Tang.) When the moving qi is above, one must not cause sweating; if one sweats it, qi will rush upward, right at the heart end, (Ligen Tang) one must not purge; if one purges it, there will be heat and vexation in the palms, body heat, sweating, and a desire to pour water over oneself. (Zhuye Tang.) When the moving qi is below, one must not cause sweating; if one sweats it, there will be no sweat, great vexation of the heart, pain in the bones and joints, headache, dizziness of the eyes, aversion to cold, and vomiting of food; (first take Da Chenpi Tang, then take Xiao Jianzhong Tang) one must not purge; if one purges it, there will be abdominal fullness, sudden dizziness upon rising, passing clear grain in the stool when eating, and a hard mass below the heart.
